A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PeKit and the same central personalization study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original PeKit recognition, captioning and image/video VQA results, together with appendix ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds threshold-sensitivity results and a physical robot demonstration.

M1.justification: The core extraction, retrieval and visual-prompting algorithm remains unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds a robotics adaptation integrating PeKit labels with OpenVox/MORE mapping and planning, ROS communication, and SAM-refined masks for rule-based grasping.

E1.justification: The existing image, multi-concept and video benchmark coverage is retained. v4 Appendix D.4 adds a targeted physical search-and-fetch scenario in which a mobile robot locates and grasps a personalized milk carton in an unfamiliar environment.

E2.justification: Corresponding recognition, captioning, VQA and ablation comparisons retain the same comparator membership, including MyVLM, Yo’LLaVA, LLaVA and the video-model baselines. Newly discussed PVIT and fingerprint-based personalization methods are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 Appendix A.4 introduces a threshold-sweep evaluation measuring precision, recall and F1 on Yo’LLaVA. The existing benchmark settings, including the fixed threshold of 0.75, model backbones and prompting procedures, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 expands the threshold analysis with sensitivity and precision–recall curves and adds the robotics case study. Earlier encoder, reference-count, object-count, naming and semantic-category ablations remain, as do the noisy-mask and small-object failure examples; several are relocated.

E5.justification: v4 Section 4.1 newly states that MyVLM accuracies are averaged over five runs. v3 gives no run count. This is additional reporting; the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs, and uncertainty intervals are not added.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, ablation and runtime values are retained apart from display rounding. New results include threshold-dependent performance and best F1 = 0.821 at threshold 0.75 in Figures 8–9, plus successful personalized milk-carton retrieval in Appendix D.4 and Figure 15.

T1.justification: The feature-pooling, memory and retrieval definitions in Equations 1–5 and the optional per-object threshold rule remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains theorems or proofs; the added threshold analysis is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free, model-agnostic personalization supporting multiple concepts and video, a challenging benchmark, and state-of-the-art performance. The additional evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v4 explains application-dependent threshold trade-offs and qualifies category-free extraction as relying on representative images with a dominant subject. Section 7 adds consent and privacy considerations. The original noisy-mask, small-object and contextual-relationship limitations are retained in main-text Section 5.

D1.justification: v4 newly documents benchmark image counts, MyVLM’s four-image training split, and exclusion of captions and negatives during view extraction. It explains threshold selection and the robot integration. The availability statement now promises both code and benchmark on GitHub, without documenting a completed release.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through text-to-image personalization, personalized retrieval and concurrent fingerprint-based training-free personalization. PVIT is added and the Hao et al. discussion is removed. MORE and OpenVox references support the new robotics application, extending the paper’s research context beyond bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: v4 substantially rewrites related work and experimental explanations, creates separate Existing Benchmarks and Ethical Considerations sections, and moves the semantic-category ablation and limitations into the main text. Earlier qualitative Appendices E–G are reorganized as D.1–D.3.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a single-column journal layout, redraws Figure 1, rearranges benchmark and failure illustrations, and splits v3 Table 3 into Tables 3–5. It adds threshold plots and a robot figure, relocates retained displays, and corrects the misleading subset descriptions in v3 Table 9’s caption, now Table 11.

improvement.justification: v4 provides empirical support for the previously unexplained fixed threshold, improves protocol disclosure, corrects the benchmark-table caption and broadens research positioning. The robot demonstration adds practical evidence, but remains an illustrative case without systematic success-rate evaluation. These gains improve clarity and support while leaving the central benchmark evidence largely unchanged.
